title: The Bus Stop on the Other Side
scene: On a chilly morning, the narrator notices a bus stop across the street and nearly rushes over, then checks the route sign and decides to stay put.
sceneJa: 寒い朝、道路の向こうのバス停を見て移動しかけるが、路線表示を確かめて今いる場所にとどまる。

chunks.en: I was running a little late,
and the bus stop across the road
chunks.ja: 道路の向こうのバス停のほうが

chunks.en: I was tempted to cross over,
chunks.ja: 向こうへ渡りたくなったが、

chunks.en: but something about the route number

chunks.ja: つじつまが合わなかった。

chunks.en: was for buses heading the other way.
chunks.ja: 反対方向のバス用だった。

chunks.en: and watched a bus pull up
chunks.ja: ちょうど立っていた場所に
バスが到着するのを見た。
10秒間動かなかったおかげで
10分の遠回りをせずに済んだ。

questions.question: Which is the natural chunk for 「その場にとどまる」?
questions.explanation: Stay put is a fixed expression meaning remain where you are.

questions.question: What does 'didn't add up' mean here?
options: つじつまが合わなかった
questions.explanation: Something doesn't add up means it seems inconsistent or suspicious.

questions.question: Why does the narrator say 'For once'?
options: To show this is not their usual experience
questions.explanation: For once suggests an unusual, slightly self-mocking success.

speak: In 30 seconds, describe a time you nearly went the wrong way. Use 'didn't add up', 'took a closer look', and 'stayed put'. Explain what you noticed and how it ended.
review: New: didn't add up（つじつまが合わなかった）, take a closer look（よく見る）, stay put（その場にとどまる）. Review: I was tempted to（〜したくなった）, sure enough（案の定）. Read aloud: pause after 'didn't add up'; emphasize 'stayed put'; deliver the last line with a dry smile.
